KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding:
AL6-03. CR-65's header caption box is printed "Court Case Number" with "(Assigned by Clerk)" directly beneath it. This packet writes matter.case_number into that box on nine of its eleven pages and leaves the identical box empty on the other two, and nothing in the held record says which case number the box is asking for.

What I measured in the delivered bytes. The caption box is filled on CR-65 pages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 (AcroForm fields Text1, Text4, Text7, Text5, "Court Case Number", "Court Case Number_2" and "Court Case Number_4") and on C-10-CRIMINAL pages 1 and 2 ("Court Case Number" and "Court Case Number_2"). It is empty on CR-65 page 7, the certificate of service, where the field is CR-65:Court Case Number_3 at x=445.44 y=691.32 w=129.00 h=35.33 - the same x origin and the same 129.00pt width as "Court Case Number_2" on page 6 and "Court Case Number_4" on page 8, both of which are filled - and empty again on C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 (C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3). So the omission is not a different field or a different box; it is the same box on two of eleven pages. Both blanks are refused in production-field-map.json with role "protected" and refusalClass "signature_or_date_participant_completion", reason "signature or date field; never prefilled", which is not a true description of a caption box and, because the class is protected, keeps both out of the participant's "Blanks you must fill in" list. I rastered both pages of the boundary fixture at 150 dpi and looked at them: page 1 shows CC-2024-000001.99 sitting directly above the printed words "(Assigned by Clerk)"; page 7 shows an empty ruled box in the same position.

The fact that makes this a real question rather than a tidy-up. CR-65 page 1 separately prints its own line, "COURT CASE NUMBER TO BE EXPUNGED:", with its own field (CR-65:Text3, x=257.20 w=287.32), and this packet fills that line with the same matter.case_number value it puts in the caption box. Two differently labelled places on the same page therefore receive the same number. If the form already has a dedicated line for the case number to be expunged, the separately labelled caption box marked "(Assigned by Clerk)" is most naturally the expungement case the clerk opens on filing - a number that does not exist yet when the packet is generated and that no participant fact can supply. But that is a reading of Alabama court-form practice, not a fact recorded anywhere in this repository, and this lane will not author it.

Why the held record cannot settle it. AL.memo.json track al-diversion records rules.filing, rules.fees, rules.feeWaiver, rules.notice, rules.service, rules.participantSignature and rules.notarization, and not one of them addresses the caption box. No participantInput on the track collects an expungement case number, and none distinguishes the underlying criminal case number from a clerk-assigned one. The packet's own field map offers no justification either: the nine writes carry factId matter.case_number with no decision or authority recorded, and the two refusals carry a reason that is false of the field.

Either answer leaves a defect; only its direction is open. If the box means the expungement case number the clerk assigns, then nine pages of this packet - including CR-65 pages 1 through 6, which the petitioner swears to under penalty of perjury on page 6 - carry a number that is not the number the box asks for, and the repair is to stop writing all nine and name the box as clerk-completed. If the box means the underlying criminal case, then CR-65 page 7 and C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 are wrongly blank, the page-7 refusal reason is false, and the repair is to write those two and reclassify them. The defect is certain; which repair is correct is not, and this lane does not choose between them. AL6-01 and AL6-02 are both genuinely gone from these bytes, and every other proof obligation this lane can settle from the record passes, so AL6-03 is the whole of the hold.

What would unblock it. A legal-design answer recorded in AL.memo.json - not in a lane return, a build script or a status file - stating whether CR-65's "Court Case Number (Assigned by Clerk)" caption box takes the underlying criminal case number or the expungement case number the clerk assigns on filing, and whether the same answer governs the identically captioned box on C-10-CRIMINAL. An owner or Alabama counsel establishing that one sentence makes the remaining work mechanical: whichever way it goes, the fix is a field-map change plus a refusal-class correction on CR-65:Court Case Number_3 and C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3, and the packet can then be rebuilt and independently re-read. Nothing else about these six families is waiting on it.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding:
AL6-03. CR-65's header caption box is printed "Court Case Number" with "(Assigned by Clerk)" directly beneath it. This packet writes matter.case_number into that box on nine of its eleven pages and leaves the identical box empty on the other two, and nothing in the held record says which case number the box is asking for.

What I measured in the delivered bytes. The caption box is filled on CR-65 pages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 (AcroForm fields Text1, Text4, Text7, Text5, "Court Case Number", "Court Case Number_2" and "Court Case Number_4") and on C-10-CRIMINAL pages 1 and 2 ("Court Case Number" and "Court Case Number_2"). It is empty on CR-65 page 7, the certificate of service, where the field is CR-65:Court Case Number_3 at x=445.44 y=691.32 w=129.00 h=35.33 - the same x origin and the same 129.00pt width as "Court Case Number_2" on page 6 and "Court Case Number_4" on page 8, both of which are filled - and empty again on C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 (C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3). So the omission is not a different field or a different box; it is the same box on two of eleven pages. Both blanks are refused in production-field-map.json with role "protected" and refusalClass "signature_or_date_participant_completion", reason "signature or date field; never prefilled", which is not a true description of a caption box and, because the class is protected, keeps both out of the participant's "Blanks you must fill in" list. I rastered both pages of the boundary fixture at 150 dpi and looked at them: page 1 shows CC-2024-000001.99 sitting directly above the printed words "(Assigned by Clerk)"; page 7 shows an empty ruled box in the same position.

The fact that makes this a real question rather than a tidy-up. CR-65 page 1 separately prints its own line, "COURT CASE NUMBER TO BE EXPUNGED:", with its own field (CR-65:Text3, x=257.20 w=287.32), and this packet fills that line with the same matter.case_number value it puts in the caption box. Two differently labelled places on the same page therefore receive the same number. If the form already has a dedicated line for the case number to be expunged, the separately labelled caption box marked "(Assigned by Clerk)" is most naturally the expungement case the clerk opens on filing - a number that does not exist yet when the packet is generated and that no participant fact can supply. But that is a reading of Alabama court-form practice, not a fact recorded anywhere in this repository, and this lane will not author it.

Why the held record cannot settle it. AL.memo.json track al-misd-conviction records rules.filing, rules.fees, rules.feeWaiver, rules.notice, rules.service, rules.participantSignature and rules.notarization, and not one of them addresses the caption box. No participantInput on the track collects an expungement case number, and none distinguishes the underlying criminal case number from a clerk-assigned one. The packet's own field map offers no justification either: the nine writes carry factId matter.case_number with no decision or authority recorded, and the two refusals carry a reason that is false of the field.

Either answer leaves a defect; only its direction is open. If the box means the expungement case number the clerk assigns, then nine pages of this packet - including CR-65 pages 1 through 6, which the petitioner swears to under penalty of perjury on page 6 - carry a number that is not the number the box asks for, and the repair is to stop writing all nine and name the box as clerk-completed. If the box means the underlying criminal case, then CR-65 page 7 and C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 are wrongly blank, the page-7 refusal reason is false, and the repair is to write those two and reclassify them. The defect is certain; which repair is correct is not, and this lane does not choose between them. AL6-01 and AL6-02 are both genuinely gone from these bytes, and every other proof obligation this lane can settle from the record passes, so AL6-03 is the whole of the hold.

What would unblock it. A legal-design answer recorded in AL.memo.json - not in a lane return, a build script or a status file - stating whether CR-65's "Court Case Number (Assigned by Clerk)" caption box takes the underlying criminal case number or the expungement case number the clerk assigns on filing, and whether the same answer governs the identically captioned box on C-10-CRIMINAL. An owner or Alabama counsel establishing that one sentence makes the remaining work mechanical: whichever way it goes, the fix is a field-map change plus a refusal-class correction on CR-65:Court Case Number_3 and C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3, and the packet can then be rebuilt and independently re-read. Nothing else about these six families is waiting on it.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding:
AL6-03. CR-65's header caption box is printed "Court Case Number" with "(Assigned by Clerk)" directly beneath it. This packet writes matter.case_number into that box on nine of its eleven pages and leaves the identical box empty on the other two, and nothing in the held record says which case number the box is asking for.

What I measured in the delivered bytes. The caption box is filled on CR-65 pages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 (AcroForm fields Text1, Text4, Text7, Text5, "Court Case Number", "Court Case Number_2" and "Court Case Number_4") and on C-10-CRIMINAL pages 1 and 2 ("Court Case Number" and "Court Case Number_2"). It is empty on CR-65 page 7, the certificate of service, where the field is CR-65:Court Case Number_3 at x=445.44 y=691.32 w=129.00 h=35.33 - the same x origin and the same 129.00pt width as "Court Case Number_2" on page 6 and "Court Case Number_4" on page 8, both of which are filled - and empty again on C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 (C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3). So the omission is not a different field or a different box; it is the same box on two of eleven pages. Both blanks are refused in production-field-map.json with role "protected" and refusalClass "signature_or_date_participant_completion", reason "signature or date field; never prefilled", which is not a true description of a caption box and, because the class is protected, keeps both out of the participant's "Blanks you must fill in" list. I rastered both pages of the boundary fixture at 150 dpi and looked at them: page 1 shows CC-2024-000001.99 sitting directly above the printed words "(Assigned by Clerk)"; page 7 shows an empty ruled box in the same position.

The fact that makes this a real question rather than a tidy-up. CR-65 page 1 separately prints its own line, "COURT CASE NUMBER TO BE EXPUNGED:", with its own field (CR-65:Text3, x=257.20 w=287.32), and this packet fills that line with the same matter.case_number value it puts in the caption box. Two differently labelled places on the same page therefore receive the same number. If the form already has a dedicated line for the case number to be expunged, the separately labelled caption box marked "(Assigned by Clerk)" is most naturally the expungement case the clerk opens on filing - a number that does not exist yet when the packet is generated and that no participant fact can supply. But that is a reading of Alabama court-form practice, not a fact recorded anywhere in this repository, and this lane will not author it.

Why the held record cannot settle it. AL.memo.json track al-misd-dwop records rules.filing, rules.fees, rules.feeWaiver, rules.notice, rules.service, rules.participantSignature and rules.notarization, and not one of them addresses the caption box. No participantInput on the track collects an expungement case number, and none distinguishes the underlying criminal case number from a clerk-assigned one. The packet's own field map offers no justification either: the nine writes carry factId matter.case_number with no decision or authority recorded, and the two refusals carry a reason that is false of the field.

Either answer leaves a defect; only its direction is open. If the box means the expungement case number the clerk assigns, then nine pages of this packet - including CR-65 pages 1 through 6, which the petitioner swears to under penalty of perjury on page 6 - carry a number that is not the number the box asks for, and the repair is to stop writing all nine and name the box as clerk-completed. If the box means the underlying criminal case, then CR-65 page 7 and C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 are wrongly blank, the page-7 refusal reason is false, and the repair is to write those two and reclassify them. The defect is certain; which repair is correct is not, and this lane does not choose between them. AL6-01 and AL6-02 are both genuinely gone from these bytes, and every other proof obligation this lane can settle from the record passes, so AL6-03 is the whole of the hold.

What would unblock it. A legal-design answer recorded in AL.memo.json - not in a lane return, a build script or a status file - stating whether CR-65's "Court Case Number (Assigned by Clerk)" caption box takes the underlying criminal case number or the expungement case number the clerk assigns on filing, and whether the same answer governs the identically captioned box on C-10-CRIMINAL. An owner or Alabama counsel establishing that one sentence makes the remaining work mechanical: whichever way it goes, the fix is a field-map change plus a refusal-class correction on CR-65:Court Case Number_3 and C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3, and the packet can then be rebuilt and independently re-read. Nothing else about these six families is waiting on it.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.detail: AL6-04, new here and decisive. CR-65 Section V is a conjunctive sworn certification - "AND ALL OF THE FOLLOWING HAVE OCCURRED. If you have not checked all eight boxes, the conviction is not eligible for expungement" - and the packet ticks all eight on the participant's behalf: Check Box10.6 on page 3 and Check Box11.0 through 11.6 on page 4, all under factId route.selection, on a petition sworn on CR-65 page 6. I rastered page 4 and read the eight printed lines against AL.memo.json track al-pardoned-felony. That track records eligibleDispositions ["a felony conviction for which a pardon has been granted"], exclusions [] (empty), waitingPeriods [] (empty), and only four participantInputs: pardonDate, restorationLanguage, firearmRightsExcluded, countyOfFiling. Six of the eight ticks therefore assert facts the route never establishes and never asks about: 11.1 "One hundred eighty days have passed from the date of the issuance of the certification of pardon" (no waiting period is recorded at all); 11.2 "the conviction is not a violent offense, as provided in Section 12-25-32"; 11.3 "not a sex offense, as provided in Section 15-20A-5"; 11.4 "not an offense involving moral turpitude, as provided in Section 17-3-30.1 ... and I have not been arrested for any offense, excluding minor traffic violations, 15 years prior to the filing of the petition"; 11.5 "not a serious traffic offense, as provided in Article 9 of Chapter 5A of Title 32"; 11.6 "At the time of the offense, I was not operating a commercial motor vehicle or was not holding a commercial driver license or commercial learner permit". A seventh, 11.0 "All civil and political rights that were forfeited as a result of the conviction have been restored", is contradicted by the track's own stop condition "The pardon withholds firearm rights and the restoration question controls" - the route expressly contemplates that this box may be false. Only 10.6, the certificate of pardon with restoration of civil and political rights, is the route's defining disposition. The comparison that proves this is not a general objection to conjunctive ticking: the sibling al-misd-conviction-set ticks its seven Section II boxes and every one of those seven IS backed by a memo exclusion, waiting period or participant input. Here six are backed by nothing. The eight-box list is source-authored, hardcoded as FAMILY_CONFIG["al-pardoned-felony-set"].selected in scripts/build-census-v1-al-diversion-set.mjs line 56, and assertRepairInvariants checks nothing about whether a ticked box is supported by the record. Telling the participant in step 3 to "confirm every condition printed in CR-65 Section V" does not cure ink already sworn on their behalf. This is the AL6-01 defect class - a semantically unsupported write into a sworn field - surviving the AL6-01 repair, with all nine counters at zero.
